description:
Hey Reachy is an unofficial app for the Reachy Mini desktop robots, native on Apple Vision Pro. It is not Pollen Robotics' own app, and it is not affiliated with, endorsed by or supported by Pollen Robotics or Hugging Face.

STEER THE ROBOT WITH YOUR HEAD

Switch on Follow my head, and the robot turns, nods and tilts its head with yours. Its body stays still, and each movement stays inside the reach of its motors. Look straight ahead when you switch it on: that direction becomes straight ahead for the robot. Watch through the robot's camera in the app's window while you look around.

visionOS gives an app the position of the headset only in an immersive space, so the app opens an empty one while Follow my head is on. The room and the app's window stay in view. Other apps' windows hide until you switch it off.

It talks to a robot on your own network directly, with no account to create. A Hugging Face sign-in is optional — for installing robot apps, and for reaching your robots from outside their network through its relay.

TRY IT WITHOUT A ROBOT

Under Developer on the Connect screen, "Start the simulator" opens a session with a robot the app carries itself — no robot, no network, no account. It is drawn from the robot's own description and moved by the same kinematics the app sends to real hardware. It has no camera, no app catalogue and no Wi-Fi setup, because those belong to a machine that does not exist. Follow my head works with it too: the 3D robot turns its head with yours.

A Reachy Mini Wireless on your network is what the whole app is for. A Lite model — or a daemon run in simulation on a computer — connects the same way, minus the routes only the wireless daemon serves.

WHAT IT DOES

• Connect — Nearby finds robots on your network with a sweep and Bonjour or at an address you type. Remote reaches the robots linked to your Hugging Face account, wherever they are.

• Live control — joystick or game controller teleop of the 6-DoF head, the antennas and body rotation, with the robot's camera and two-way audio, so you can talk through its speaker. Let the head follow a face, at a strength you pick between a glance and a lock.

• 3D viewer — a RealityKit model built from the robot's own URDF and meshes, mirroring it in real time.

• Moves — browse and play the recorded moves the robot ships with, from the app or by asking Siri for one by name. Record your own takes with the joystick and play them back.

• Sounds — a soundboard for the robot's speaker: add audio files from your device and play them with a tap.

• Apps — install, update and remove robot apps from Hugging Face Spaces, following each job as it runs. Filter and sort the catalogue, pin the apps you use most, report an app or hide its author.

• State and logs — the control loop's frequency, worst interval and error count charted live. The daemon's log streams in as it is written.

• Setup and recovery — put a brand-new robot onto Wi-Fi over an encrypted Bluetooth channel, guide its first wake-up, or bring back one that fell off the network.

ON APPLE VISION PRO

Siri and Shortcuts for waking, sleeping, powering off, launching an app, playing a move, or asking whether the robot is awake and what is running on it, each able to name which robot it means. Six accent themes, each with a colour for the 3D robot. English, German, Spanish, French and Russian.

PRIVACY

Nothing is collected. The app talks to your robot and, if you sign in, to Hugging Face with your own account. There is no server on our side.

A NOTE ON YOUR NETWORK

The robot's daemon provides no authentication and no encryption of its own. Use Hey Reachy on a trusted private network or on the robot's own access point — never through a port forward or a public address.

Hey Reachy is an independent client for the robot daemon's documented HTTP and WebSocket API. "Reachy Mini" is a product name of Pollen Robotics, used here solely to describe what this app is compatible with.

Requires visionOS 26.
promotionalText: Turn your head, and Reachy Mini turns its own. Watch through its camera, drive it with a joystick or a game controller, or try the simulator inside the app.
